title: Your first HTML document
goals: Write a valid HTML5 document from DOCTYPE to closing html
Use h1, p, and a correctly
Open a local HTML file in the browser and see the result
bodyMd:
## A page is just a text file HTML is not a programming language. It is a **markup** language: you label parts of a document so the browser knows what they mean. Every modern page starts with the same skeleton. ### The minimum valid page ```html Hello Doyintech Academy

Hello, web

This is my first page.

``` ### What each part does | Piece | Role | |-------|------| | `` | Tells the browser to use HTML5 rules | | `` | Root element; `lang` helps screen readers and SEO | | `` | Metadata — title, charset, viewport — not visible as page text | | `` | Everything the user sees | | `

` | Main heading (one primary h1 per page is a good habit) | | `

` | Paragraph | ### Charset and viewport - **charset utf-8** — so Nigerian names, currency symbols, and emoji render correctly. - **viewport** — so the page does not look zoomed-out on phones. ### Links ```html Visit DoyinTech ``` `href` is the destination. The text between the tags is what the user clicks. ### Try it offline 1. Create a folder `first-page`. 2. Save the skeleton as `index.html`. 3. Double-click the file (or drag it into Chrome). 4. You should see your heading — no server required yet.

practice.prompt: Create index.html with your name in the h1, one paragraph about why you are learning to code, and a link to any site you use daily. Open it in the browser.
practice.solution: A valid page with title, h1 with your name, at least one p, and one a[href].

quiz.question: Where does visible page content belong?
quiz.explain: The body holds what users see. Head is for metadata.

quiz.question: Why set charset to utf-8?
choices: So a wide range of characters render correctly
It replaces the need for a title
quiz.explain: UTF-8 supports most written languages and symbols.

quiz.question: What does the viewport meta tag help with?
quiz.explain: Viewport tells mobile browsers how to size the layout viewport.

video.script: In this lesson you will write your first real HTML file — not a screenshot, a file you own. We will walk the skeleton: doctype, html, head, body. Then you will add a heading, a paragraph, and a link, and open it in the browser. By the end you will know that a website starts as plain text with clear labels.
